newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech fund KB Plus sees 1996 net loss.
newsitem.headline: Czech fund KB Plus sees 1996 net loss.

text.p: The Czech fund IKS KB Plus on Wednesday reported a preliminary net loss for 1996 of 524 million crowns due to a re-evaluation of the fund's portfolio, after a 102 million crown profit for 1995.

"As a result of the re-evaluation of the administratively-installed prices of shares from the second wave of coupon privatisation, the fund ended with a (1996) loss in the amount of 524 million crowns," Jindirch Vodenka, the fund's manager from IKS Komercni Banka, said in a statement.
He said the loss would be covered out of set-aside reserves for such a purpose.
Czech funds have been forced to re-value their portfolio to take account of the shares from the country's coupon privatisation programme which were originally entered in accounts at nominal value.
Vodenka said that despite the loss, the fund's managers still planned to pay a gross 7.5 crown dividend per unit on 1996 earnings, up from the seven crown dividend paid for the previous year.
The fund's total assets at the end of 1996 were 1.897 billion crowns, up from 1.67 billion at the end of 1995.
